title: The Next Phase of Value-Based Care: Why Specialty-Led Models Will Define the Future of Healthcare
summary: More than three-quarters of health system and hospital executives plan to expand participation in value-based care (VBC) models over the next two years, up from 57% in 2023. But despite growing momentum, value-based care has yet to fully deliver on its promise of improving patient health while reducing costs. Unlocking the promise of value-based care Value-based care offers a path to sustainably reduce healthcare costs while keeping patients healthier.

summary: In medical innovation, we prioritize evidence, outcomes, and economics. Metrics such as clinical endpoints, regulatory milestones, reimbursement pathways, and market opportunities define our progress. Yet, hope is a powerful driver of medical innovation.

summary: Pharmaceutical companies often point to slow clinical trial enrollment as a chokepoint for drug development, but it’s no picnic for patients either. Physicians may be able to suggest a trial or two, but it’s hard for them to keep up with all of the drugs in clinical development, said Tran Le, co-founder of Grove AI. Grove’s technology uses AI agents to automate many clinical trial recruitment tasks that have historically been handled by a human.

title: Daffodil Health Launches No Surprises Act Dispute Management Solution
summary: Daffodil Health, an AI health plan administration platform, unveiled a new solution on Thursday that aims to help payers manage No Surprises Act disputes. The No Surprises Act shields patients from unexpected medical bills by keeping them out of payment disputes between insurers and providers. Daffodil’s new NSA dispute management solution aims to solve this issue.

title: STAT+: Novo Nordisk inflammation-targeting drug misses mark in heart disease study
summary: Novo Nordisk said Friday that its investigational anti-inflammatory drug did not reduce the risk of major heart events in a pivotal trial, raising questions about the increasingly popular approach of targeting inflammation to prevent cardiovascular complications. In a Phase 3 study that enrolled over 6,300 people with heart disease, kidney disease, and inflammation, the drug, ziltivekimab, did lower markers of inflammation, Novo said. However, that did not translate into a reduction in risk of major complications, including cardiovascular-related death, heart attack, or stroke.

summary: Nine years ago in these pages, we — columnists for STAT at the time — praised the American Diabetes Association for standing up to a researcher in Brazil who had sued the group in U.S. federal court for issuing expressions of concern on four of his published articles. We even named the ADA the inaugural winner of our Doing the Right Thing award. It’s time the ADA brought back the justifiable swagger of 2015.

title: Why Hims & Hers Is Embroiled in Yet Another Controversy, This Time with the FTC
summary: After making amends in its dispute with Novo Nordisk over the sale of compounded GLP-1s, telehealth company Hims & Hers is tied up in yet another legal battle. The Federal Trade Commission, along with Utah and California, sued Hims & Hers on Wednesday, arguing that the telehealth company unlawfully shared consumers’ health information with third-party advertising platforms and deceived customers about its billing and cancellation practices. The FTC alleged that Hims & Hers has misled “hundreds of thousands of consumers” by charging them for unwanted medication subscriptions without their consent.

title: J&J Joins Immune Reset Race, Paying $785M to Partner on Sail Bio Cell Therapy
summary: Johnson & Johnson, which was part of the wave of the first cell therapies, is now getting a next-generation contender by paying $785 million to start a partnership on a Sail Biomedicines cell therapy in development for autoimmune disorders. In addition to gaining access to Sail’s lead program and the platform technology that created it, J&J secured an exclusive option to acquire the startup. At the time, Sail said it would advance SAIL-0804 to the clinic.

summary: Is the Food and Drug Administration taking inconsistent approaches to Duchenne muscular dystrophy drugs? How will a new batch of drug executives shake up their companies? Allison, Elaine, and Adam discuss Capricor Therapeutics’ hearing in front of an FDA advisory committee .

title: Key Senate panel backs Trump’s picks for CDC, pandemic preparedness
summary: WASHINGTON — The Senate health committee approved two nominees for key health roles Thursday, including the director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and a pandemic preparedness leader, after Chair Bill Cassidy (R-La.) once again set aside his reservations to support Trump administration leadership picks. The vote on Erica Schwartz for CDC director was approved by all Republicans and by Tim Kaine (D-Va.), with other Democrats opposed. Cassidy heavily criticized Kaufman for these remarks during the hearing, and Kaufman endorsed vaccines during his opening statement.

title: More Medications, Less Clarity: Strengthening Polypharmacy Support for CKD Patients
summary: In chronic kidney disease (CKD), medication adherence depends on coordinated, interdisciplinary care that helps patients manage complex regimens, avoid preventable errors, and improve long-term outcomes. Medication adherence is central to CKD care. When care teams as a whole are more involved in a patient’s care, it can improve these outcomes.

summary: BOSTON — In an order issued Thursday, a federal judge denied 26 states’ request to postpone the implementation of Medicaid work requirements announced in June. The case seeks to alter a piece of one of President Trump’s biggest legislative priorities. But states must also communicate with Medicaid recipients by Aug.

summary: The war with Iran has driven oil prices up, prompting concern that the supply of some medicines will be disrupted. But there is another consideration. title: Moving Beyond Reactive Healthcare: 5 Traits of Successful Healthcare Organizations
summary: A new white paper from League highlights how healthcare organizations are transforming the way they manage untenable healthcare costs with innovative tech collaborations from maternal health to improving the way they care for high-risk patients to developing AI tools in-house targeting internal needs. Among the five traits the white paper highlights are: ● Accountability for long-term health outcomes ● Treating the consumer experience as a performance lever ● Enabling teams with the best tools ● Using data effectively ● A willingness to flip the old model The white paper exolores the concept of an infinite care team using a coordinated system of AI agents working across benefits navigation, care gap closure, health coaching, and care navigation. It addresses frequently asked questions such as what does a consumer’s health plan actually cover, when they are due for check-ups, and how they can stay healthy.

title: STAT+: Tracking the FDA expert review of Replimune’s melanoma treatment
summary: Welcome to STAT’s live blog of a meeting, convened by the Food and Drug Administration, to review Replimune’s experimental treatment for melanoma . The FDA’s Cellular, Tissue, and Gene Therapies Advisory Committee is meeting Thursday to evaluate whether the biotech company has collected sufficient data to support the accelerated approval of RP1, an engineered viral immunotherapy for melanoma. Investors have interpreted the FDA’s decision to hold an advisory committee meeting about the drug as a sign of new lenience.

summary: When I met Tesfaye at Boru Meda General Hospital, he vaguely remembered the thorn. He was 15 when it pricked his foot, out in the fields somewhere in Mekdela, in north-central Ethiopia. Mycetoma is a disease of poverty.

summary: Starting next week, Nebraskans on Medicaid will be at risk of losing their health coverage unless the state can verify that they work, volunteer, or attend school for 80 hours per month. Come January, millions of other low-income Americans will face the same cliff. Their health care coverage may be at risk, at a time when many patients can’t afford such interruptions.

title: Doctronic Acquires Summer Health to Expand into Pediatric Primary Care
summary: Doctronic, an AI-powered primary care company, announced Wednesday that it is expanding into pediatric care through the acquisition of virtual pediatric company Summer Health. New York City-based Doctronic provides free health insights. The deal will also strengthen Doctronic’s AI capabilities with Summer Health’s repository of 100,000 pediatric text messages.

title: Processa Acquisition Lands Immunology Drug That Could Rival a New Novartis Product
summary: Processa Pharmaceuticals is reshaping its pipeline with the acquisition of Vidya Therapeutics , a clinical-stage biotech whose main asset is a molecule that offers broad potential in immune-mediated disorders ranging from rare inflammatory skin diseases to common food allergies. The deal announced Wednesday is an all-stock transaction. Processa describes Vidya’s drug as a next-generation BTK inhibitor.

title: NSF testing new Ph.D. model giving trainees academic and industry experience
summary: Young life scientists have been increasingly abandoning academia , a seismic shift that has fueled calls for rethinking graduate education. On Wednesday, the Trump administration announced that it’s funding a pilot program to test a new strategy: Giving Ph.D. students industry experience — and dollars — as part of their training. UIDP started brainstorming how to change that in 2021, drawing inspiration from existing university-industry Ph.D. programs in Europe as well as a program at Lehigh University in Pennsylvania.

title: STAT+: Latigo reports mid-stage success for would-be rival to Vertex’s pain drug Journavx
summary: For decades, efforts to develop non-opioid pain drugs were marked by failure. But what was once a graveyard of drug discovery is quickly turning into a race for a multibillion-dollar market, with Latigo Biotherapeutics publishing positive data on Wednesday for a therapy meant to rival a Vertex medicine already on the market. Those given either dose of Latigo’s oral drug, LTG-001, showed statistically significant pain relief compared to placebo after 48 hours.

title: Epic-First Doesn’t Mean Epic-Only: Where Hospitals Are Still Buying from Startups
summary: Epic ‘s grip on hospital IT is tightening — yet a surprising number of health systems say they’re still willing to buy elsewhere. This week, Redesign Health released research proving this. Hospitals are also willing to select an outside vendor when Epic’s product in a given category just isn’t strong enough yet.

title: STAT+: Hims misled consumers and violated their privacy, FTC alleges in a lawsuit
summary: On Wednesday, the Federal Trade Commission sued direct-to-consumer telehealth company Hims & Hers, continuing a pattern of action against digital health companies’ business practices and use of consumer health data. The FTC, along with Utah and California, alleged that Hims deceived consumers in several ways when they purchased clinical care and medications through the site. The telehealth company misled consumers about sharing their sensitive health information with third parties including Meta and Snap, the suit claims.

title: STAT+: End of Medicare drug subsidy gives Democrats new attack line on rising out-of-pocket costs
summary: WASHINGTON — The Trump administration will end subsidies for private Medicare drug plans, likely resulting in higher premiums for some older adults right before the midterm elections. Democrats were already campaigning on the approximately $1 trillion in health care cuts in Republicans’ tax bill from last summer . They immediately seized on the decision to end drug plan subsidies as another opportunity to attack Republicans on affordability.

title: A New Era of Interoperability, But Who Gets Left Behind?
summary: CMS released its Interoperability Framework in 2025 as a path forward for EMRs to finally make seamless data exchange a reality. The vision is clear: empower patients and providers by building a connected infrastructure that’s open, standards-based, and rooted in execution instead of theoretical debate. CMS is trying to make it work.

title: The Healthcare Cloud Maturity Model: The Five Stages Most Health Systems Skip
summary: Most health systems will tell you they are “in the cloud.” What that usually means is that they moved a rack of on-premise servers into a cloud provider’s data center, kept the application architecture exactly as it was, and then watched the monthly bill climb instead of fall. Being in the cloud, in that sense, is a little like a car being in a garage. Stage three: Cloud-native refactoring.

title: Fauci invokes Fifth Amendment in declining to answer questions before Senate panel
summary: At a highly anticipated Senate hearing , Anthony Fauci on Wednesday invoked his Fifth Amendment right to refuse to answer questions about the Covid-19 pandemic and its origins, saying he was doing so on the advice of his attorneys. By the end of the event, after the infectious disease expert declined to answer a single question from lawmakers, Rand Paul, the Kentucky Republican who forced Fauci to appear, announced that he would convene a vote next week on whether to hold Fauci in contempt for his refusal. Paul has made no secret of his desire to see Fauci behind bars.

title: STAT+: FDA expert panel recommends against approval of Capricor’s Duchenne drug
summary: A group of outside experts convened Wednesday by the Food and Drug Administration concluded clinical data for a treatment for Duchenne muscular dystrophy from Capricor Therapeutics did not provide “substantial evidence” of efficacy. The vote was 9-3, sending to the FDA a recommendation that the Capricor treatment, called deramiocel, should not be approved. The voting question centered on whether the drug had shown it could treat Duchenne-related cardiomyopathy.

title: Opinion: The VA could help America win the biotechnology race with China
summary: Biotechnology is rapidly becoming a pillar of national power. The nation that can discover, test, and deploy new therapies most efficiently will not only improve the health of its citizens but also shape global standards, attract investment, strengthen military readiness, and dominate one of the most important industries of the past century. Real-time clinical development is therefore much more than a regulatory innovation — it is a strategic capability.

title: STAT+: In the biotech industry, a most-wanted fugitive was long hiding in plain sight
summary: When one of Rhode Island’s most-wanted fugitives was discovered last week to have been secretly working under an alias in the biotech industry , the reaction among many was shock. How did he evade scrutiny for two decades? And how did the companies that hired him — at least one biotech on a full-time basis and at least two large pharmaceutical companies on a contractual basis — not vet him more thoroughly?

title: STAT+: Clinical chatbots are taking medicine by storm. Should doctors trust them?
summary: Hundreds of thousands of U.S. doctors use clinical large language models, pitched by companies like OpenEvidence, Doximity, and UpToDate as an antidote to the dangers of hallucination-prone generalist models from Big Tech. Yet few studies have pitted them against each other — and this summer brought a high-profile head-to-head. Researchers from NYU Langone Health had tested general and clinical models, including OpenEvidence and UpToDate Expert AI, on three sets of clinical questions.

title: STAT+: American Diabetes Association, facing calls for resignations, asks for patience
summary: The expulsion of five diabetes experts from the American Diabetes Association meeting last month continues to reverberate, with more than 200 members now calling for two ADA leaders to resign. In response, the ADA delivered its own message Tuesday, expressing appreciation for members’ patience while a report is prepared. The resignation demand, sent last week in an open letter to the ADA board of directors, calls for the removal of CEO Charles Henderson and chief scientific and medical officer Rita Kalyani.

title: Smart Toilet Sensor Startup Is Flush with $10M Funding
summary: More than six in ten Americans had some sort of symptom signaling poor digestive health in just the past week, yet most still have no way to track what’s happening in the bathroom. On Tuesday, an Austin-based startup seeking to help solve that problem closed its Series A round. Though it’s an early category, Throne isn’t without competition.

title: Included Health to Acquire Firefly Health to Expand Alternative Health Plan Offering for Employers
summary: Included Health, a navigation and virtual care company, announced Tuesday that it plans to acquire Firefly Health, a primary care and health plan provider. San Francisco-based Included Health provides virtual and in-person care, navigation and care coordination and 24/7 support for clinical and administrative needs. The acquisition will accelerate Included Health’s alternative plan strategy for employers, according to Owen Tripp, CEO of Included Health.

title: Altimmune’s GLP-1 Drug Reduces Heavy Drinking in Alcohol Use Disorder Trial
summary: GLP-1 drugs first made their mark in diabetes and obesity, but many research efforts are underway to bring such therapies to more indications. Altimmune now has mid-stage clinical trial results showing its molecule designed to target two gut hormone receptors led to a reduction in alcohol consumption . Altimmune’s pemvidutide pairs GLP-1 agonism with the activation of glucagon receptors.

title: Six key issues we’re watching at Fauci’s hearing
summary: WASHINGTON — Senate Republicans, and particularly Rand Paul (R-Ky.), have long been critical of the government’s actions during the Covid-19 pandemic — which began during the first Trump administration — and have sought to pin blame on those they believe played some role in the virus’s outbreak and what they describe as a subsequent cover-up of the pandemic’s origins. On Wednesday, they will again get another chance to explore the past when Anthony Fauci, the nation’s former top infectious disease expert, testifies before the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee following a subpoena issued by Paul. Fauci is clearly aware of the risk.

title: Visa time limits on foreign Ph.D. students and postdocs will harm U.S. science, experts warn
summary: For nearly half a century, the federal government encouraged international students and scholars to study in the U.S. by allowing them to stay for the duration of their training — regardless of how many years it took. The Trump administration now plans to tear up that long-standing policy, fueling concerns in the research community that the U.S. could lose out on talented foreign scientists. The average biomedical Ph.D. takes five to six years to complete, meaning a majority of incoming foreign graduate students would need to apply for DHS extensions to complete their work.

title: STAT+: Bracing for another Fauci hearing
summary: You’re reading the web edition of D.C. Diagnosis, STAT’s twice-weekly newsletter about the politics and policy of health and medicine. Also, join STAT’s Isabella Cueto and Lev Facher tomorrow at 1 p.m.

title: STAT+: GSK lays out plans to cut costs, pursue more late-stage drug trials
summary: LONDON — Half a year into taking over the job, GSK CEO Luke Miels on Tuesday laid out his plans to turn the U.K. pharma giant into a more agile company with years of growth ahead. A key step, Miels said, will be a three-year campaign to generate 1.9 billion pounds (about $2.5 billion) in annual savings by 2029, much of which will be reinvested to advance the company’s late-stage pipeline. The company also now plans to start at least 20 Phase 3 trials this year, up from the 10 that it had disclosed at the beginning of 2026. “We are step-by-step building a set of potential best-in-class products across our core therapy areas,” Miels said, a list that includes some newer target areas — like oncology and liver disease — as well as longtime GSK focuses like vaccines and HIV.

title: STAT+: FDA staff reiterate concerns about Replimune skin cancer treatment
summary: Regulators at the Food and Drug Administration have reiterated concerns that Replimune does not have adequate data to support an approval of its investigational skin cancer treatment, as the biotech tries for the third time to seek clearance for its highly controversial drug. In briefing documents released Tuesday ahead of a meeting of FDA advisers later this week, the agency took issue with the single-arm trial the biotech relies on, in which patients who have already tried a PD-1-inhibitor took Replimune’s drug, called RP1, in combination with the PD-1-inhibitor Opdivo. Replimune counters in its own briefing document that “it is not feasible or ethical” to conduct a study that randomly assigns its drug or placebo on top of PD-1 inhibitors in patients whose cancer has stopped responding to PD-1s, since “there is no evidence that continued anti-PD-1 monotherapy provides any level of clinical benefit” to those patients.

title: Why Specialized UM Delivers on Every NICU Outcome
summary: It’s the latest industry recommendation: that health plans move routine Utilization Management (UM) in-house and leave complex, specialty care to the experts . As both a nurse and a clinical operations leader, I couldn’t agree more. Neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admissions are clinically complex.

title: Spotting Alzheimer’s Years Earlier Through AI and Clinically Meaningful Insights
summary: For decades, Alzheimer’s disease has been detected far too late. By the time memory and thinking problems disrupt daily life, underlying biological changes have often been progressing quietly for years . Brain health assessment is approaching a moment of practical transformation.

title: Why Endeavor Health Refuses to Silo Its Value-Based Care Strategy
summary: Value-based care has become one of the most misunderstood terms in the healthcare industry, according to Lakshmi Halasyamani, chief clinical officer at Endeavor Health . She said hospitals tend to treat value-based care as another payment arrangement — but it’s really more of a commitment to patients. “I think we have to evolve on the health system side — shift from it being based on a contractual relationship to it really being about our promise to the people who we’re caring for. That’s the perspective shift Halasyamani wants to see across the sector — from value-based care as a payment mechanism to value-based care as a genuine understanding of who a patient is outside the exam room.

title: Argenx’s $2B Forte Bio Acquisition Brings Autoimmune Playbook to Prevalent Disorders
summary: Argenx established itself in immunology with a single drug offering potential use across a range of rare inflammatory disorders. The biotech is now expanding to more prevalent conditions through a $2.2 billion deal to buy Forte Biosciences, a company whose lead asset has encouraging clinical data in two common conditions with few treatment options. The Forte acquisition complements Argenx’s portfolio, Massey said.

title: Prior Authorization Is Draining Revenue: Why Automation Has Become a Strategic Imperative
summary: Prior authorization has become one of healthcare’s most expensive administrative bottlenecks , affecting far more than physician practices. Across hospitals and health systems, it slows patient access, adds labor-intensive work, increases denial risk, and puts pressure on reimbursement and cash flow. Prior authorization is becoming a strategic capability issue, not just an administrative burden.

title: How AI Inside Clinical Workflows Is Unlocking Patient Throughput
summary: U.S. hospitals may be on the brink of a capacity crisis. A 2025 JAMA Network Open study found that average U.S. hospital occupancy now runs at 75%, up roughly 11 percentage points from the pre-pandemic baseline near 64%. The data hospitals need to improve patient throughput already exists.

title: AI Readiness Starts with Solving Healthcare’s Data Fragmentation Problem
summary: Healh insurers are interested in assessing the potential for AI to improve everything from prior authorization to member management. But data fragmentation poses an enormous challenge to AI readiness in healthcare for both payers and provider health plans. Thomasina Anane, Associate Vice President of Enterprise Analytics for the Alliance of Community Health Plans , highlighted the need for shared data definitions and consistent data governance.

title: What Happens When Patients Trust AI Over Their Doctor?
summary: Patients are increasingly walking into exam rooms having already consulted an AI chatbot about their symptoms — and sometimes trusting it as much as they trust their doctor. But when a chatbot gets it wrong and a patient gets hurt, who bears the responsibility? Once a patient starts discussing AI-generated information during a clinical encounter, that information becomes part of the clinical picture the same way as a patient reporting web-browsing results or advice from their friend, O’Connor noted.

title: Crystalys Therapeutics Tacks On $130M for Pivotal Tests of Gout Drug
summary: Crystalys Therapeutics does not yet have data from pivotal tests of its gout drug, but the company is already looking ahead to potentially bringing the drug to the market, plans supported by a fresh $130 million in capital . The new financing announced last Wednesday comes less than a year after Crystalys launched, revealing an in-licensed gout drug candidate and a $205 million Series A round. Frazier Life Sciences led Crystalys’s Series B financing.

title: Candid Health Snags $120M for AI RCM Platform
summary: Candid Health, a revenue cycle management platform, announced Wednesday that it raised $120 million in Series D funding. San Francisco-based Candid Health serves medical groups, managed service organizations and digital health companies. In total, Candid Health has raised about $219 million.

title: Why Value-Based Care Only Works If You’ve Tamed Costs
summary: Across the country, community and mid-size hospitals are facing a new financial reality: a shift to a riskier payer mix. Commercial coverage that once cross-subsidized care is shrinking, Medicare is growing, and Medicaid “churn” is pushing more patients into uninsured status. Evaluating these common opportunities for cost containment is a critical step for hospitals considering a value-based care model.

title: Medicine Understands Trauma’s Impact, But Rarely Asks About It
summary: The United States is in the middle of a mental health crisis marked by surging rates of depression, anxiety, and suicidal ideation. A recent JAMA study revealed that pediatric primary care visits for anxiety climbed to more than three times their previous rate since 2016, and one in five adolescents report significant mental health challenges. Emotional distress and trauma, whether experienced in childhood or adulthood, directly dictate health outcomes across a person’s life course.

title: A Prescription for Drug Costs: Inject Transparency and Improve Accessibility
summary: Drug research continues to churn out new advances, some that are potential cures. But even though more than $800 billion a year is spent on pharmaceuticals, many Americans either don’t get the medicines they need or for various reasons, they can’t. “A quarter to a third of adults skip or ration their medications because of the cost of medications, which we find unacceptable,” said Jay Rughani, partner at Andreesen Horowitz. “And this is increasingly putting pricing pressures on the demand side, on the employer side, and on the payer side, and on the government side of how we’re thinking about making these medicines affordable.” Rughani’s comments came as moderator of a drug costs panel during MedCity News’ Bullseye conference in Chicago on Thursday. Another friction point is lack of price transparency.

title: What Health Tech Investors Love in Founders — and What They Can’t Stand
summary: Digital health investors have heard nearly every founder pitch imaginable, including many that start along the lines of “healthcare is broken, and I’m the one who’s going to fix it.” During a panel this week at MedCity News ’ Bullseye event in Chicago three healthcare investors made it clear that this kind of certainty is often a warning sign, not a selling point. What they’re actually looking for is closer to its opposite — founders who are confident enough to have conviction, but self-aware enough to know what they don’t know. Lisa Carmel, chair of business development at Mayo Clinic , agreed that self-awareness is often the deciding factor, especially for founders who haven’t built a company before. “That incredibly valuable skill of being self-aware and recognizing their blind spots,” Carmel said, is what separates founders worth backing from those who aren’t.

title: Priority Health Launches 2 Cancer Support Solutions with Color Health, Grail
summary: Priority Health, a Michigan-based insurer, announced Wednesday that it has launched two new cancer support solutions for employers in partnership with Color Health and Grail. The insurer serves more than 1.4 million members in Michigan, Indiana, Ohio and Wisconsin. With the new solutions, Priority Health’s employer customers can offer cancer navigation, support and screening through Color Health’s virtual cancer clinic, as well as early cancer detection through Grail’s blood test.

title: AI Will Reshape the Patient Experience
summary: Nearly no one got into the business of health care because they want to think about identity. But AI is making us all rethink healthcare, and quickly. As exciting as this new world is, it raises a whole new set of identity questions.

title: Healthcare’s Next Source of Alpha Is Moving Upstream
summary: Healthcare venture investing has always been a competition to identify the best companies. This next decade will belong to the investors identifying the best breakthroughs before they become companies at all. By Series A, the strongest healthcare companies often attract dozens of investors.

title: CRISPR Biotech Scribe Therapeutics Writes a New Chapter With $129M IPO
summary: For many people, managing a disease means chronic therapy. Scribe Therapeutics has a different vision: genetic medicines that offer durable effects for the masses. Both are co-founders of Scribe.

title: Healthcare Investors Are Rewriting the ROI Playbook from Cost-Cutting to Cash Flow
summary: Healthcare has weathered tech-driven capital waves before, like the dot-com boom or the dawn of DNA sequencing — but this one is different, according to a panel of four investors. During a session Thursday at MedCity News ’ Bullseye event in Chicago, these investors laid out why AI is the first healthcare tech wave that is succeeding at actually generating new revenue instead of just cutting costs. Another panelist — Carter Prince, a partner at CVS Health Ventures — agreed, noting that AI’s relative accessibility is opening up entirely new customer segments.

title: Who Broke the Healthcare System?
summary: It’s often said that the healthcare system is broken, from the outdated use of fax machines to perverse incentives. But who broke the healthcare system? The response? “We did,” replied Sachin Jain, CEO of SCAN Health Plan , referring to all of those who work inside of healthcare.

title: Rethinking How Hospitals Measure Behavioral Health Success
summary: Two patients who present in the emergency department in identical ways can have very different treatment experiences, even if they’re both assessed within the standard window and discharged within the target length-of-stay. Both treatments would appear normal in an operations dashboard. Most hospitals rely on emergency department behavioral health metrics that can’t tell these two patients apart.

title: Four Ways Health Systems Should Plan for the Next Wave of Breakthrough Therapies
summary: Within the next three to five years, the drug pipeline is expected to continue to boom with specialty medications dominating the list. Specialty medications are high-cost prescription medications used to treat complex medical conditions such as multiple sclerosis, cystic fibrosis, oncology and inflammatory diseases. Specialty pharmacy plays a unique role in helping hospitals prepare for these new therapies while also connecting patients to breakthrough therapies.

title: Snapchat creates ad format to support pharma disclosure needs
summary: Snapchat is courting pharma marketers with a new ad format designed to support the disclosure needs of branded prescription drug campaigns. Advertisers on Snapchat, a social media platform on which posts are only available for a short period of time, can add calls to action (CTAs) at the bottom of their posts. Snapchat has adopted a multi-CTA model to help pharma marketers.

title: CytoDyn’s leronlimab reaffirms HIV potential after combo treatment eradicates virus in infant macaques
summary: CytoDyn's leronlimab may have struggled to secure approval as an HIV treatment, but research in infant primates has offered fresh hope for the CCR5-targeting antibody's ability to treat the virus. The latest findings, published August 10 in Nature Microbiology , come from a study of 55 infant macaques that received different combinations of three drugs—broadly neutralizing antibodies (bNabs), antiretroviral therapy and leronlimab. For the study, researchers infected infant macaques orally with HIV virus and then began administering a treatment regimen 72 hours later.

title: Deerfield-backed Boulevard Bio embarks on ‘beautiful path to a cure’ with trio of immunology drugs
summary: Boulevard Bio has strolled out of stealth with $65 million in funding from Deerfield Management and three autoimmune disease candidates. The New York-based biotech is focused on B cell biology and was incubated by Deerfield Discovery and Development (3DC), the investment firm's internal therapeutics and research development engineer, according to an August 12 release. Further back in Boulevard’s own pipeline is BLVD201, a trispecific CD19/BCMA/CD3 T-cell engager (TCE) designed to treat severe B cell-driven autoimmune diseases.

title: Definium hits another phase 3 homerun with psychedelic ‘sea change’ for anxiety
summary: Definium Therapeutics’ LSD formula has gone two for two in its phase 3 program, notching a win in generalized anxiety disorder mere months after knocking a depression study out of the park. The 214-patient Voyage trial pitted a psychoactive session with Definium’s DT120 ODT against placebo, with the psychedelic coming out ahead by reducing anxiety symptoms at week 12 by 11.6 points compared to a 6.2-point reduction for placebo. Symptom severity was assessed using the Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAM-A). “We have never seen a pivotal study deliver greater than five-point placebo-adjusted change on the HAM-A, and we did this 12 weeks after a single dose of drug,” Definium CEO Robert Barrow told Fierce.

title: Samsung hearing aid features for its ear buds garner FDA clearance
summary: The FDA gave Samsung Electronics the go-ahead for the latest software features that allow its Galaxy Buds earphones to act as an OTC hearing aid that also allows users to diagnose their hearing. The hearing test feature is registered as a software for medical device and provides medical-grade results, the company said in an August. The regulatory agency officially opened the door to prescription-free hearing aid tech in 2022.

title: Attruby cruises toward blockbuster land as BridgeBio CEO spots ‘stabilizer-first’ ATTR market
summary: As Alnylam’s Amvuttra sales disappointed, revenue from BridgeBio’s rival transthyretin amyloidosis (ATTR) drug Attruby came in above analysts’ expectations. With Attruby’s $222 million in second-quarter U.S. sales beating Wall Street consensus by 6%, Jefferies analysts expect the ATTR stabilizer could surpass the $1 billion mark in annual global sales this year. BridgeBio has been targeting about 30% to 40% of the overall ATTR-CM market share.

title: WuXi AppTec scores temporary win amid fight over DOD's Chinese military company brand
summary: Arguing that the Defense Department might have misread evidence and inflicted harm on the company, a federal judge has thrown WuXi AppTec a lifeline as the research and manufacturing services juggernaut fights its recent classification by the U.S. government as a Chinese military company. Late last week, a judge with the U.S. WuXi AppTec and its sister CDMO WuXi Biologics have faced repeated scrutiny from China hawks in the U.S. government in recent years.

title: Aura lays off 20% of workforce, rejigs C-suite amid R&D refocus on eye cancer
summary: Aura Biosciences is refocusing under its recently installed CEO, laying off 20% of its employees and overhauling its C-suite as the Boston biotech narrows its focus on ocular oncology. Natalie Holles, who took over as CEO in April, inherited a company focused on developing precision therapies to treat solid tumors. Aura unveiled new chief operating, chief regulatory and quality, and chief people officers.

title: Abbott teams with Google Health on AI-powered health insights app
summary: Two giants of their respective fields, Abbott and Google, are joining forces for a first-of-its-kind team-up to build a digital picture of people’s health. The partnership will wed Abbott’s Lingo consumer glucose wearable with Google Health’s AI technology to generate “personalized metabolic insights” via the Google Health app. The study will integrate continuous glucose monitoring, wearable, laboratory and survey data to examine connections between activity, sleep, well-being and metabolic health, with the goal of informing more personalized health guidance.

title: Zydus’ Sentynl pens $475M deal for Mereo’s phase 3-ready rare genetic lung disease drug
summary: Sentynl Therapeutics has penned a deal potentially worth $475 million for the option to market Mereo BioPharma's phase 3-ready rare genetic respiratory disease drug in the U.S. In return for an undisclosed upfront payment, Sentynl—a subsidiary of Zydus Lifesciences—has secured the option to commercialize alvelestat in the U.S. Mereo acquired alvelestat from AstraZeneca for $5 million upfront back in 2017.

title: Epicrispr raises $90M to rewrite treatment of rare muscle disease
summary: Epicrispr Biotechnologies has raised $90 million in a series C round backed by investors including Sanofi Ventures, positioning the biotech to advance a pipeline of epigenetic medicines led by an early-phase facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD) prospect. San Francisco-based Epicrispr began a phase 1/2 trial of the FSHD drug candidate, EPI-321, last year. The series C round cements Epicrispr as a rider in the race to treat FSHD, which currently lacks approved therapies.

title: Amgen lays groundwork for new R&D center in Hyderabad
summary: Amgen is expanding its footprint in India with an R&D center in Hyderabad, the latest effort from the California company to boost its research facilities. The new Science and Innovation Center is set to open in Hyderabad’s Genome Valley, a biopharma business park, in 2027, an Amgen spokesperson told Fierce in a statement. By setting up camp in Genome Valley, Amgen will be surrounded by many familiar faces.

title: ‘We are proud to be in the lead’: Vaderis lands $152M for phase 3 study in rare blood vessel disorder
summary: Vaderis Therapeutics has secured an oversubscribed $152 million series B financing to propel the Swiss biotech's AKT inhibitor through phase 3 with the aim of bringing the first treatment for a rare blood vessel disorder to market. The Basel-based company has just launched the late-stage study to evaluate the once-daily oral drug, called engasertib, in patients with hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT). Meanwhile, Atavistik Bio kicked off a phase 1/2 trial last month in partnership with the Cure HHT clinical trial network to assess an oral allosteric AKT1-selective inhibitor for HHT.

title: Regeneron backs $75M series A for antibody upstart Infinimmune
summary: Infinimmune has amassed further fuel to power its antibody discovery engine, netting a $75 million series A headlined by Regeneron’s venture arm. Regeneron Ventures co-led the Bay Area biotech’s fundraise alongside Playground Global, with other newcomers like RA Capital Management, Forge Life Science Partners and Goldcrest Capital also pitching in. Existing investors came back for the series A too, including Infinimmune’s partner, Merck & Co. “As a company working in eczema, we're thrilled to have Regeneron Ventures co-leading our financing,” Infinimmune co-founder and CEO Wyatt McDonnell, Ph.D., told Fierce.

title: Abbott casts telenovela star Gabriela Spanic to take the drama out of colon cancer screening
summary: Abbott has enlisted telenovela star Gabriela Spanic to push the message that getting screened for colon cancer doesn’t have to be dramatic. Spanic is known for telenovelas such as “La Usurpadora,” a 1998 hit TV show in which she played twin sisters with diametrically opposed characters. Now, Abbott is leveraging Spanic’s star power to encourage more Latino adults to be screened for colon cancer.

title: Unapproved in US for decades, levosimendan stumbles in phase 3 as Tenax eyes narrow FDA path
summary: Nearly three decades after its failed bid for FDA approval, the cardiovascular drug levosimendan is still struggling to secure a decisive clinical win to enter the U.S. market. In the latest chapter of the drug’s U.S. odyssey, Tenax Therapeutics reported that an oral version of levosimendan missed the primary endpoint of a phase 3 trial, leaving the biotech to rely on subgroup data to chart a narrow path forward with the FDA. U.S. rights to levosimendan then landed at Tenax.

title: Trump signs executive order to overhaul pediatric vaccine recommendations
summary: President Donald Trump signed an executive order Monday that calls for reducing the number of required vaccinations for children in a move that backs a revised immunization schedule pushed by the Department of Health and Human Services. The executive order recommends immunizing children against 11 diseases, rather than the 17 that are currently recommended by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). The order outlines three distinct categories of childhood immunization recommendations: vaccines recommended for all children, immunizations recommended for certain high-risk groups or populations and immunizations based on shared clinical decision-making.

title: Inizio Engage expands medical information digs with Connected Insights platform
summary: Inizio’s Engage arm is widening its global medical information offerings with its new ‘Connected Insights’ platform. The new expansion merges regional expertise in the Asia-Pacific market, enhanced global infrastructure and AI-enabled innovation to help medical affairs teams deliver high-quality medical information at a global scale, Inizio explained in its press release . “Medical Information has become one of the richest sources of scientific insight across the product lifecycle,” Inizio Engage’s VP of global medical information Jenny Reid-Young commented in the release. “Organizations that can connect those interactions across markets and translate them into meaningful intelligence will make better decisions, improve customer experiences and strengthen Medical Affairs strategy. Inizio Engage is one arm of Inizio’s five connected businesses, which includes Inizio Evoke, Inizio Ignite, Inizio Medical and Inizio Biotech.

title: Quanterix hires GE Healthcare, Exact Sciences alum as chief commercial officer
summary: Quanterix Corporation has hired medtech veteran Jim Gute as its new chief commercial officer. Gute comes to the testing company from Exact Sciences, where he was senior vice president and commercial manager of general screening. Cunningham previously worked at both Exact Sciences and GE Healthcare.

title: Bristol Myers Squibb lays out plan for $2.3B manufacturing facility in Houston
summary: Everything is bigger in Texas. And so it is with Bristol Myers Squibb’s $2.3 billion investment in a manufacturing campus in Houston, which comes in at more than twice the price the company estimated in a government application earlier this year. In the BMS release, Texas Gov.

title: Labcorp nabs FDA green light for BRAF melanoma diagnostic
summary: The FDA has signed off on Labcorp’s companion diagnostic for patients with advanced melanoma carrying certain BRAF variants. The PGDx elio tissue complete CDx is now approved in the U.S. to help identify patients with advanced melanoma, the deadliest type of skin cancer, who may benefit from targeted treatments. Those include BRAF inhibitors such as Novartis’ Tafinlar and Roche’s Zelboraf for patients with BRAF V600E mutations, as well as BRAF/MEK inhibitor combination regimens for patients with V600E or V600K mutations.

title: Sionna’s cystic fibrosis flop sends stock down 90%, but a ‘significant positive’ for Vertex
summary: Sionna Therapeutics has axed a cystic fibrosis add-on program after flunking a phase 2 trial, eliminating a would-be challenger to Vertex Pharmaceuticals’ empire. The biotech plans to “take actions to preserve capital while evaluating next steps.” Massachusetts-based Sionna has emerged as a potential threat to Vertex in recent years, tapping private and public investors to fund development of internal candidates and assets licensed from AbbVie. Sionna linked SION-719 to a mean placebo-adjusted reduction in sweat chloride of 1.0 mmol/L.

title: Scholar Rock ditches Novo’s legacy Catalent plant in FDA refiling of SMA drug
summary: Scholar Rock has shed Novo Nordisk’s troubled Catalent facility as a contract manufacturer in its FDA refiling for apitegromab, a candidate for spinal muscular atrophy. The Cambridge, Massachusetts-based biotech announced the move Friday, while assuring investors of the FDA’s target decision date of Sept. The decision comes a year after problems at the legacy Catalent fill-finish facility in Bloomington, Indiana, triggered a complete response letter for Scholar Rock’s original application for apitegromab.

title: Jazz pays $820M to buy Actio, adding clinical-stage asset to orchestra of epilepsy therapies
summary: Jazz Pharmaceuticals is adding to its orchestra of epilepsy treatments with the acquisition of Actio Biosciences for $820 million upfront. The prize for Jazz is Actio’s lead asset, dubbed ABS-1230, a small-molecule precision therapy targeting the KCNT1 ion channel. ABS-1230 has already demonstrated “meaningful seizure reductions” in an early clinical proof-of-concept trial in children with KCNT1+ epilepsy, Jazz explained in an August 10 release .

title: MoonLake’s nanobody boosts all clinical endpoints in phase 3 psoriatic arthritis trial
summary: MoonLake Immunotherapeutics announced positive phase 3 data of patients with psoriatic arthritis treated with its lead nanobody candidate, sonelokimab. At week 16, 42.1% of patients achieved American College of Rheumatology 50 (ACR50), or at least a 50% improvement in rheumatoid arthritis symptoms such as joint pain and swelling. Psoriatic arthritis is a chronic inflammatory disease that causes joint pain, swelling, and stiffness.

title: ITM neuroendocrine tumor drug spurned by FDA over manufacturing qualms
summary: The FDA has denied ITM Isotopes Technologies’ lead pipeline candidate for a rare group of tumors due to qualms over the drug’s manufacturing. The FDA’s complete response letter did not raise any issues with ITM-11’s clinical or safety data, ITM clarified. ITM is also testing ITM-11 in a slew of other trials, including a phase 3 study for a different subset of patients with GEP-NETs.

title: aTyr lays off 60% of workforce to fund 2nd attempt at phase 3 success for lung disease drug
summary: Sixty per cent of aTyr Pharma’s workforce are heading for the exits as the biotech conserves resources for a second shot at phase 3 success in a type of lung disease. Last year, aTyr revealed that its immunomodulator efzofitimod had missed the primary endpoint in a late-stage study for people with moderate-to-severe forms of the inflammatory lung disease (ILD) pulmonary sarcoidosis. That remains the plan, with aTyr having submitted a protocol for its next planned phase 3 study to the FDA in July.

title: Arpeggio plays final chord as biotech disbands on poor prospects for Nrf2 program
summary: Arpeggio Biosciences’ eight-year song has come to an end as the transcriptome biotech’s CEO admitted the company’s Nrf2 program had started to “unravel.” The Boulder, Colorado-based biotech was set up by CEO Joey Azofeifa, Chief Technology Officer Tim Read and Chief Operating Officer Laura Norris in 2018 to make use of what Arpeggio claimed at the time was the “largest database of nascent-RNA sequences in the world.” The company’s research had its origins at the University of Colorado’s BioFrontiers Institute. Armed with a $17 million series A in 2022 from the likes of Builders VC, Khosla Ventures and TechU Ventures, the company’s focus became a small molecule Nrf2 degrader for non-small cell lung cancer. Arpeggio’s website is no longer accessible and it’s unclear how many employees will be affected by the company’s closure.

title: Sobi pens $580M deal for Innate’s skin cancer drug ahead of phase 3 push
summary: Sobi has bought into Innate Pharma’s vision for lacutamab, handing the French biotech $75 million upfront for the rights to market the anti-KIR3DL2 antibody for an aggressive skin cancer. Innate has already secured a green light from the FDA to test lacutamab in the phase 3 Tellomak-3 study for cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (CTCL), ahead of a planned approval push in a subtype of CTCL called Sézary syndrome. In return, Sobi gets exclusive global rights to commercialize lacutamab for Sézary syndrome, assuming the phase 3 trial is a success.

title: Silence brings the noise to Takeda with phase 2 blood cancer win
summary: A phase 2 trial of Silence Therapeutics’ divesiran has hit its primary endpoint, emboldening the biotech to gear up for late-phase development of a potential challenger to Takeda and Protagonist Therapeutics’ rusfertide. The biotech designed divesiran, a siRNA drug candidate, to treat a rare blood cancer characterized by the excessive production of red blood cells. Silence plans to administer divesiran every 12 weeks in its phase 3 trial.

title: Novo Nordisk and Amazon sign AI drug discovery pact, launch London innovation hub
summary: Novo Nordisk and Amazon Web Services (AWS) will partner to leverage AI and accelerate drug discovery. The deal will result in AWS becoming Novo’s preferred cloud provider and AI partner while creating a hub inside the Big Pharma's existing London facility where the two companies will collaborate on how to accelerate the development of new medicines, according to an August 10 release. The Danish Big Pharma will also deploy Amazon Bedrock AgentCore—a managed infrastructure platform to help developers deploy and scale AI agents—in an effort to make its operations more efficient. “Every part of our work with Novo Nordisk comes back to one thing: getting the right medicine to patients, faster,” AWS CEO Matt Garman said in the release. “We’re excited to partner with Novo Nordisk so that these technologies, AWS forward deployed engineers and Novo Nordisk’s industry-leading science teams can help compress drug discovery timelines, securely process complex datasets and scale findings across therapeutic areas.” The pact is an extension of Novo’s ongoing collaboration with Amazon, which also includes Amazon Pharmacy, Amazon Ads and Amazon One Medical throughout its business functions.

title: FDA issues alert in wake of BD recall of faulty needle sets that caused four deaths
summary: The FDA’s Center for Devices and Radiological Health issued an early alert for Becton Dickson’s Intraosseous Vascular Access system needle sets in the wake of four deaths and 45 serious injuries related to the product. A CDRH early alert is a warning from the regulatory agency for patients and physicians not to use a medical device that has the potential for high-risk outcomes before a formal recall classification is determined. BD issued a recall letter July 30 that use of the needle sets be discontinued immediately and all affected lots be destroyed or quarantined until disposal, the agency said in its alert.

title: AbCellera women’s health data top ‘most aggressive upside scenario,’ putting Astellas and Bayer on notice
summary: AbCellera has reported phase 2 results “beyond even the most aggressive upside scenario” that its CEO dared to consider, boosting the biotech’s chances of challenging Astellas and Bayer for a women’s health market. The phase 2 clinical trial compared ABCL635, an antibody targeting NK3R, to placebo in patients with hot flashes caused by menopause. By Week 4, the number of moderate or severe hot flashes had fallen by a mean of 8.8 on ABCL635 and by 3.5 on placebo.

title: The Next Frontier in Patient Support: Connected Data, AI and Personalized Engagement
summary: Patient support programs generate vast amounts of data, yet many life sciences companies still struggle to translate information into timely, meaningful action. Despite significant investments in patient support programs and digital engagement, outcomes remain stubbornly slow: Up to one-third of patients never start their prescribed treatment, and 30% of patients say diagnostic delays worsened their condition. As healthcare shifts toward more proactive and personalized models of care, the challenge is no longer data collection.

title: Fresenius Kabi recalls mislabeled morphine lot that could cause overdose death
summary: Fresenius Kabi voluntarily recalled one lot of morphine sulfate injection due to a labeling mix-up with prefilled syringes of the opioid dilaudid that could trigger an overdose resulting in severe respiratory distress or death. The recall, issued in a letter dated Aug. The lot was distributed nationwide to distributors and wholesalers.

title: Novo Nordisk makes Omnicom agency of record for US media buying
summary: Novo Nordisk has made Omnicom the agency of record for U.S. media buying, ending the drugmaker’s six-year partnership with WPP’s Wavemaker. Omnicom will manage Novo’s media buying in the U.S. starting in the fourth quarter, Liz Skrbkova, who leads U.S. media and stakeholder relations at the Danish drugmaker, told Fierce Pharma Marketing. In 2019, Novo reported (PDF) GLP-1 diabetes sales of 33.2 billion Danish krone ($5.1 billion).

title: AbbVie’s Skyrizi retakes edge in pharma’s July ad spending league
summary: AbbVie retook the top spot from rival Johnson & Johnson and its immunology drug Tremfya in July’s top TV drug ad spending rankings. That’s according to data shared with Fierce Pharma Marketing from iSpot.TV, which saw AbbVie boost spending on its blockbuster med by $6 million when compared to June.
